item.title: We Were at AIM26
item.description:
We were at AIM26 this year and had a great time meeting physics students and introducing the ASGARD group :)

The AIM (Working Group Inspiration Fair) is an annual information fair organized by the Fachschaft, aimed at connecting physics students with research groups. Its primary purpose is to provide students with the opportunity to speak directly with researchers in order to find opportunities for Bachelor’s or Master’s theses and student research assistant positions (HiWi jobs).

Thanks to everyone who helped make our participation possible! Special thanks go to Ole and Benedikt for representing the group at the stand :)

item.title: Work by Seok-Jun Chang featured on the MPA webpage
item.description:
Work by former group member Seok-Jun Chang has been featured on the Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics (MPA) website: https://www.mpa-garching.mpg.de/1147117/hl202605

The MPA highlight, titled “Radiative Transfer Shapes Hydrogen Lines in Little Red Dots”, presents results on how resonance, Raman, and Thomson scattering shape hydrogen emission lines in Little Red Dots and discusses the implications for interpreting these systems.

The featured work is based on the paper by Seok-Jun Chang, Max Gronke, Jorryt Matthee, and Charlotte Mason on hydrogen line formation in Little Red Dots.

Links to paper:

  • https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/staf2131
  • https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08768

item.title: Fernando Hidalgo Pineda receives UMass-BW scholarship
item.description:
Fernando Hidalgo Pineda has been selected for a research stay at the University of Massachusetts Amherst in fall 2026, through the Baden-Wurttemberg-UMass coordinated by the University of Hohenheim.

He has been awarded a scholarship funded by the Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts, Baden-Wurttemberg, to support the visit. Congratulations, Fernando!

item.title: Numerical/Theoretical Journal Club started!
item.description:
We have started a weekly Numerical/Theoretical Journal Club, organized by Caitlin Doughty and Fernando Hidalgo-Pineda. The club meets every Monday, 14:00–14:30 in the library lounge of ARI. Sessions are informal; everyone is welcome.

To be added to the mailing list, for questions or to suggest papers, contact the organizers.

item.title: Silvia Almada Monter wins Kippenhahn Prize
item.description:
The Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics (MPA) has awarded the Rudolf-Kippenhahn-Prize for the best scientific paper by a student to Silvia Almada Monter.

Silvia received the award for her paper titled “Crossing walls and windows: the curious escape of Lyman-α photons through ionized channels”. Her research challenges existing assumptions about how Lyman-alpha photons escape from galaxies, proposing a new physical picture.

The prize recognizes originality, scientific impact, and the quality of writing in publications where students made substantial contributions.

item.title: Our Group has moved to ARI/ZAH
item.description:
The ASGARD research group has officially started at the Astronomisches Rechen-Institut (ARI) at the Zentrum für Astronomie der Universität Heidelberg (ZAH).

We are excited to be part of this vibrant research environment and look forward to new collaborations and scientific discoveries.
